"""Cell 01, the infeed conveyor: the operating rules (what the agent is told), the program it is
handed, and the test suites. The seeded faults are deliberately not labelled anywhere the agent can
see; the hidden manifest used for scoring lives in agent/plc/hidden.py."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

from .lang import parse_program

SPEC = [
    {"id": "S1", "title": "E-stop stops the belt", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While the E-stop (ESTOP) is pressed, MOTOR must be off in the same scan."},
    {"id": "S2", "title": "Open guard stops the belt", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While the guard door is open (GUARD_CLOSED = 0), MOTOR must be off."},
    {"id": "S3", "title": "STOP dominates", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While STOP is pressed, MOTOR must be off, even if START is pressed in the same scan."},
    {"id": "S4", "title": "No automatic restart", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "After any stop (STOP, E-stop, guard opened, or a fault shown on LAMP_RED) the belt may only "
             "run again after a new START press (rising edge). Pausing for a box at the pick position is "
             "not a stop: the belt resumes by itself once the robot has picked the box."},
    {"id": "S5", "title": "E-stop needs a reset", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "Once the E-stop has been pressed, LAMP_RED must stay on and MOTOR off until the E-stop is "
             "released AND RESET is pressed (rising edge). A RESET press while the E-stop is still pressed does not count."},
    {"id": "S6", "title": "Stop at the pick position", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While PE_END sees a box (the pick position), MOTOR must be off in the same scan, or the box is "
             "pushed off the end of the belt (the end is 0.4 m past the point where PE_END first sees a box, "
             "which is 0.8 s at belt speed)."},
    {"id": "S7", "title": "Jam supervision", "kind": "safety", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "If PE_IN stays blocked for 3.0 s while MOTOR runs (a jam, or a stuck sensor), the conveyor must "
             "stop, latch a fault shown on LAMP_RED, and stay stopped until PE_IN is clear and RESET is pressed, "
             "then START. Checked in simulation: MOTOR and PE_IN on together for more than 3.5 s is a violation."},
    {"id": "F1", "title": "START runs the belt", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "With the guard closed, no E-stop and no fault, a START press runs MOTOR immediately."},
    {"id": "F2", "title": "Deliver and resume", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "Boxes travel to the pick position and wait there with LAMP_AMBER on; after the robot picks a box "
             "the belt resumes without a new START."},
    {"id": "F3", "title": "No false jam alarms", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "A box waiting at the infeed while the belt is stopped is normal and must never raise a fault."},
    {"id": "F4", "title": "Lamps", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "LAMP_GREEN = belt running; LAMP_AMBER = in run mode but paused for a box at the pick position; "
             "LAMP_RED = E-stop latched or fault."},
]

SIGNALS_DOC = """Inputs: START, STOP, RESET (momentary push buttons, 1 while pressed), ESTOP (1 while the mushroom
button is pressed in), GUARD_CLOSED (1 when the interlocked guard door is closed), PE_IN (photo-eye at the
infeed, 1 when a box is in front of it), PE_END (photo-eye at the pick position).
Outputs: MOTOR (belt drive), LAMP_GREEN, LAMP_AMBER, LAMP_RED (stack light).
Plant: the belt is 4.0 m long and moves at 0.5 m/s while MOTOR = 1. Boxes are 0.4 m long, placed at the
infeed (x = 0.2 m). PE_IN sits at x = 0.3 m, PE_END at x = 3.7 m. A robot picks boxes waiting at PE_END.
The PLC scans every 0.1 s."""

LANGUAGE_DOC = """Each rung is one statement; rungs run top to bottom every 0.1 s scan.
  COIL = expr                  assign (every scan)
  SET COIL WHEN expr           latch on
  RESET COIL WHEN expr         latch off
  TON T_NAME(expr, 3.0s)       on-delay timer; T_NAME.Q is 1 once expr has been 1 for the preset time
expr uses NOT, AND, OR, parentheses, TRUE/FALSE, signal names, T_NAME.Q and RISE(X) (1 for the scan in
which X goes from 0 to 1). A coil read before the rung that writes it holds its value from the previous
scan. Inputs cannot be written. Limits: 24 rungs, 12 internal coils, 4 timers, presets 0.1-10 s,
12 contacts per rung."""

BASELINE_SOURCE = """
R01  SET ESTOP_LATCH WHEN ESTOP                 # remember an E-stop
R02  RESET ESTOP_LATCH WHEN NOT ESTOP
R03  TON T_JAM(PE_IN AND NOT MOTOR, 3.0s)       # jam supervision timer
R04  SET FAULT WHEN T_JAM.Q
R05  RESET FAULT WHEN RISE(RESET) AND NOT PE_IN
R06  RUN = (RISE(START) OR RUN) AND NOT STOP AND NOT ESTOP AND NOT ESTOP_LATCH AND NOT FAULT    # run mode, sealed in
R07  TON T_END(PE_END, 1.2s)                    # box at the pick position (debounced)
R08  MOTOR = RUN AND GUARD_CLOSED AND NOT T_END.Q
R09  LAMP_GREEN = MOTOR
R10  LAMP_AMBER = RUN AND NOT MOTOR
R11  LAMP_RED = ESTOP_LATCH OR FAULT
"""


def baseline_program() -> list[dict]:
    return parse_program(BASELINE_SOURCE)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tests
# A test is a scenario plus expectations: {"t": time, "sig": name, "val": 0/1} checked on the frame at
# that time, "min_picked": boxes the robot must have picked, and no safety violations (S1-S7, DROP).

def _press(t, name, d=0.3):
    return {"t": t, "kind": "press", "input": name, "duration": d}


def _set(t, name, v):
    return {"t": t, "kind": "set", "input": name, "value": v}


def _test(tid, title, desc, duration, events, expect, options=None, min_picked=0):
    return {"id": tid, "title": title, "description": desc, "duration": duration, "events": events,
            "options": options or {}, "expect": expect, "min_picked": min_picked}


VISIBLE_TESTS = [
    _test("V01", "Deliver one box", "START, place a box, the robot picks it, the belt keeps running.", 14,
          [_press(0.5, "START"), {"t": 1.0, "kind": "spawn"}],
          [{"t": 1.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}, {"t": 8.0, "sig": "LAMP_AMBER", "val": 1}, {"t": 12.0, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}],
          {"autopick_after": 1.0}, min_picked=1),
    _test("V02", "STOP and restart", "STOP stops the belt; START runs it again.", 7,
          [_press(0.5, "START"), _press(3.0, "STOP"), _press(5.0, "START")],
          [{"t": 4.0, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0}, {"t": 6.0, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}]),
    _test("V03", "E-stop, then START without RESET", "After an E-stop is released, START alone must not run the belt; RESET then START must.", 8,
          [_press(0.5, "START"), _set(2.0, "ESTOP", 1), _set(3.0, "ESTOP", 0), _press(4.0, "START"), _press(5.0, "RESET"), _press(6.0, "START")],
          [{"t": 2.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0}, {"t": 3.5, "sig": "LAMP_RED", "val": 1}, {"t": 4.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0},
           {"t": 5.5, "sig": "LAMP_RED", "val": 0}, {"t": 6.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}]),
    _test("V04", "Guard door opened and closed", "Opening the guard stops the belt; closing it must not restart it until START.", 7,
          [_press(0.5, "START"), _set(2.0, "GUARD_CLOSED", 0), _set(4.0, "GUARD_CLOSED", 1), _press(5.0, "START")],
          [{"t": 3.0, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0}, {"t": 4.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0}, {"t": 5.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}]),
    _test("V05", "Box stops at the pick position", "The belt must stop with the box at PE_END and not push it off the end.", 12,
          [_press(0.5, "START"), {"t": 1.0, "kind": "spawn"}],
          [{"t": 9.0, "sig": "PE_END", "val": 1}, {"t": 9.0, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0}, {"t": 9.0, "sig": "LAMP_AMBER", "val": 1}]),
    _test("V06", "Stuck infeed sensor", "PE_IN sticks on while running: the belt must stop with a fault, and recover after repair, RESET and START.", 9,
          [_press(0.5, "START"), {"t": 2.0, "kind": "stick", "sensor": "PE_IN", "value": 1},
           {"t": 7.0, "kind": "unstick", "sensor": "PE_IN"}, _press(7.5, "RESET"), _press(8.0, "START")],
          [{"t": 6.0, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0}, {"t": 6.0, "sig": "LAMP_RED", "val": 1}, {"t": 8.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}]),
    _test("V07", "Box waiting at the infeed", "A box placed while the belt is stopped must not raise a fault; START then runs the belt.", 8,
          [{"t": 0.5, "kind": "spawn"}, _press(5.0, "START")],
          [{"t": 4.5, "sig": "LAMP_RED", "val": 0}, {"t": 5.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}]),
    _test("V08", "START and STOP together", "STOP wins when both are pressed in the same scan.", 4,
          [_press(1.0, "START"), _press(1.0, "STOP"), _press(2.0, "START")],
          [{"t": 1.1, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 0}, {"t": 2.5, "sig": "MOTOR", "val": 1}]),
]

HELDOUT_TESTS = [

def fuzz_scenarios(seed: int, n: int, duration: float = 30.0) -> list[dict]:
    """Random operator and plant behaviour, for checking the safety rules beyond the scripted tests."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        t, events = 0.5, []
        estop = 0
        guard = 1
        while t < duration - 1:
            r = rng.random()
            if r < 0.30:
                events.append(_press(round(t, 1), "START"))
            elif r < 0.40:
                events.append(_press(round(t, 1), "STOP"))
            elif r < 0.50:
                events.append(_press(round(t, 1), "RESET"))
            elif r < 0.58:
                estop = 1 - estop
                events.append(_set(round(t, 1), "ESTOP", estop))
            elif r < 0.66:
                guard = 1 - guard
                events.append(_set(round(t, 1), "GUARD_CLOSED", guard))
            elif r < 0.80:
                events.append({"t": round(t, 1), "kind": "spawn"})
            elif r < 0.90:
                events.append({"t": round(t, 1), "kind": "pick"})
            elif r < 0.95:
                events.append({"t": round(t, 1), "kind": "stick", "sensor": rng.choice(["PE_IN", "PE_END"]), "value": 1})
            else:
                events.append({"t": round(t, 1), "kind": "unstick", "sensor": rng.choice(["PE_IN", "PE_END"])})
            t += rng.choice([0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0])
        out.append({"id": f"FZ{seed}-{i:03d}", "title": "random", "description": "", "duration": duration, "events": events,
                    "options": {"autopick_after": rng.choice([1.0, 2.0])} if rng.random() < 0.5 else {}})
    return out

"""Cell 01, the infeed conveyor: the operating rules (what the agent is told), the program it is
handed, and the test suites. The seeded faults are deliberately not labelled anywhere the agent can
see; the hidden manifest used for scoring lives in agent/plc/hidden.py."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

from .lang import parse_program

SPEC = [
    {"id": "S1", "title": "E-stop stops the belt", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While the E-stop (ESTOP) is pressed, MOTOR must be off in the same scan."},
    {"id": "S2", "title": "Open guard stops the belt", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While the guard door is open (GUARD_CLOSED = 0), MOTOR must be off."},
    {"id": "S3", "title": "STOP dominates", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While STOP is pressed, MOTOR must be off, even if START is pressed in the same scan."},
    {"id": "S4", "title": "No automatic restart", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "After any stop (STOP, E-stop, guard opened, or a fault shown on LAMP_RED) the belt may only "
             "run again after a new START press (rising edge). Pausing for a box at the pick position is "
             "not a stop: the belt resumes by itself once the robot has picked the box."},
    {"id": "S5", "title": "E-stop needs a reset", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "Once the E-stop has been pressed, LAMP_RED must stay on and MOTOR off until the E-stop is "
             "released AND RESET is pressed (rising edge). A RESET press while the E-stop is still pressed does not count."},
    {"id": "S6", "title": "Stop at the pick position", "kind": "safety", "method": "proof",
     "text": "While PE_END sees a box (the pick position), MOTOR must be off in the same scan, or the box is "
             "pushed off the end of the belt (the end is 0.4 m past the point where PE_END first sees a box, "
             "which is 0.8 s at belt speed)."},
    {"id": "S7", "title": "Jam supervision", "kind": "safety", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "If PE_IN stays blocked for 3.0 s while MOTOR runs (a jam, or a stuck sensor), the conveyor must "
             "stop, latch a fault shown on LAMP_RED, and stay stopped until PE_IN is clear and RESET is pressed, "
             "then START. Checked in simulation: MOTOR and PE_IN on together for more than 3.5 s is a violation."},
    {"id": "F1", "title": "START runs the belt", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "With the guard closed, no E-stop and no fault, a START press runs MOTOR immediately."},
    {"id": "F2", "title": "Deliver and resume", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "Boxes travel to the pick position and wait there with LAMP_AMBER on; after the robot picks a box "
             "the belt resumes without a new START."},
    {"id": "F3", "title": "No false jam alarms", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "A box waiting at the infeed while the belt is stopped is normal and must never raise a fault."},
    {"id": "F4", "title": "Lamps", "kind": "functional", "method": "simulation",
     "text": "LAMP_GREEN = belt running; LAMP_AMBER = in run mode but paused for a box at the pick position; "
             "LAMP_RED = E-stop latched or fault."},

SIGNALS_DOC = """Inputs: START, STOP, RESET (momentary push buttons, 1 while pressed), ESTOP (1 while the mushroom
button is pressed in), GUARD_CLOSED (1 when the interlocked guard door is closed), PE_IN (photo-eye at the
infeed, 1 when a box is in front of it), PE_END (photo-eye at the pick position).
Outputs: MOTOR (belt drive), LAMP_GREEN, LAMP_AMBER, LAMP_RED (stack light).
Plant: the belt is 4.0 m long and moves at 0.5 m/s while MOTOR = 1. Boxes are 0.4 m long, placed at the
infeed (x = 0.2 m). PE_IN sits at x = 0.3 m, PE_END at x = 3.7 m. A robot picks boxes waiting at PE_END.
The PLC scans every 0.1 s."""

LANGUAGE_DOC = """Each rung is one statement; rungs run top to bottom every 0.1 s scan.
  COIL = expr                  assign (every scan)
  SET COIL WHEN expr           latch on
  RESET COIL WHEN expr         latch off
  TON T_NAME(expr, 3.0s)       on-delay timer; T_NAME.Q is 1 once expr has been 1 for the preset time

which X goes from 0 to 1). A coil read before the rung that writes it holds its value from the previous

) -> None:
    """
    Initialize Neatlogs SDK.

    Args:
        api_key: Neatlogs API key (or set NEATLOGS_API_KEY env var)
        endpoint: Neatlogs backend endpoint (falls back to the NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT
                 env var, then https://ingest.neatlogs.com; an explicit value
                 wins over the env var)
        workflow_name: Logical grouping for traces
        user_id: Operator identifier — whoever is RUNNING the SDK (a developer, a
                 service account, the OS user). Propagates to all spans as a
                 resource attribute. NOT the end-user of your app.

                 NOTE: session and end-user identity are NOT set here. They are
                 per-request, not process-global. Set them at the trace root via
                 ``@span(kind="WORKFLOW", session_id=..., end_user_id=...)`` /
                 ``with neatlogs.trace(session_id=..., end_user_id=...)``, or for
                 wrapper-only code via ``with neatlogs.identify(session_id=...,
                 end_user_id=...)``.
        tags: Global tags for all traces (list of strings only, e.g., ['production', 'api-v2'])
        instrumentations: Specific AI/provider/framework libraries to instrument.
              HTTP clients are intentionally unsupported; trace the semantic
              operation around a raw transport call instead.
        sample_rate: Trace sampling rate (0.0-1.0)
        batch_size: Max spans per batch
        flush_interval: Seconds between batch flushes
        debug: Enable debug logging
        disable_export: Disable data export (for testing)
        capture_logs: Capture Python logging.* calls and neatlogs.log() as LOG spans.
                      Default: False. Enable to see intermediate steps in the timeline.

"""The STOP/PROVE agent loop: plan, act through tools, verify, recover, submit.

v1 is the naive first version (tests only, pass/fail answers, no verification). v2 adds failure
details, experiments on the digital twin, the model checker, regression detection and rollback."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time

from .tools import TOOL_DEFS, V1_TOOLS, V2_TOOLS, ToolFailure, Workbench

TASK = (
    "You are commissioning the control program for Cell 01, an infeed conveyor, before it is loaded into the real PLC. "
    "The program was written by a contractor and has not been verified. Make it satisfy every operating rule. "
    "Start by reading the spec and the program."
)

SYSTEM_V1 = (
    "You are a PLC programmer. Fix the program so that the tests pass, using the tools. "
    "Submit when you are done."
)

SYSTEM_V2 = """You are STOP/PROVE, a careful controls engineer agent. You commission PLC logic on a digital twin before it
touches a real machine. The program you are given has an unknown number of defects. Nobody will tell you what
they are: find them from evidence.

Method:
1. Read the spec (machine, language, operating rules) and the program.
2. Run the tests. For each failure, read the details (scan tables) and form a root-cause hypothesis that names

"""Held-out evaluation and export of runs for the web viewer (web/public/data)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from .plc.cell import HELDOUT_TESTS, SPEC, VISIBLE_TESTS, baseline_program, fuzz_scenarios
from .plc.hidden import FAULTS
from .plc.sim import run_scenario
from .plc.verify import fuzz, prove, run_suite

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DATA = ROOT / "web" / "public" / "data"
HELDOUT_FUZZ_SEED = 2026
HELDOUT_FUZZ_EPISODES = 300

# Before/After showcase scenarios (ids match the viewer's built-in ones).
SHOWCASE = [
    ("pick-overrun", "Box at the pick position", "A box rides to the robot. The belt must stop at PE_END instead of pushing it off the end.", "V05"),
    ("estop-no-reset", "E-stop, then START without RESET", "After the E-stop is released, START alone must not run the belt.", "V03"),
    ("guard-restart", "Guard door opened and closed", "Closing the guard must not restart the belt on its own.", "V04"),
    ("stuck-infeed", "Stuck infeed sensor", "PE_IN sticks on while running. The jam must be caught within 3 s.", "V06"),
    ("production", "One minute of production", "Continuous feeding and picking for 60 s.", "H06"),
]


def evaluate(program: list[dict]) -> dict:
    vis = run_suite(program, VISIBLE_TESTS)
    held = run_suite(program, HELDOUT_TESTS)
    pr = prove(program)
    fz = fuzz(program, fuzz_scenarios(HELDOUT_FUZZ_SEED, HELDOUT_FUZZ_EPISODES))
    passed = {r["id"] for r in vis + held if r["passed"]}
    proven = {r["rule"] for r in pr["results"] if r["status"] == "proven"}
    fixed = [f["id"] for f in FAULTS if all(t in passed for t in f["tests"]) and (f["rule"] not in [r["rule"] for r in pr["results"]] or f["rule"] in proven)]
    return {
        "visible": {"pass": sum(r["passed"] for r in vis), "total": len(vis)},
        "heldout": {"pass": sum(r["passed"] for r in held), "total": len(held)},
        "heldout_failed": [{"id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "why": r["failures"][0]["message"]} for r in held if not r["passed"]],
        "proofs": [
            {k: v for k, v in r.items() if k in ("rule", "status", "states_explored", "counterexample")} for r in pr["results"]
        ],
        "motor_reachable": pr["motor_reachable"],
        "fuzz": {"episodes": fz["episodes"], "violations": fz["violations"], "by_rule": fz["by_rule"]},
        "faults_fixed": {"fixed": len(fixed), "total": len(FAULTS), "ids": fixed},
    }


def _scenario_of(test_id: str) -> dict:
    t = next(x for x in VISIBLE_TESTS + HELDOUT_TESTS if x["id"] == test_id)
    return {"id": t["id"], "title": t["title"], "description": t["description"], "duration": t["duration"],
            "options": t["options"], "events": t["events"]}


def showcase_pairs(repaired: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    base = baseline_program()
    out = []
    for sid, title, desc, test_id in SHOWCASE:
        sc = _scenario_of(test_id)
        if sid == "production":
            sc["duration"] = 40
        sc = {**sc, "id": sid, "title": title, "description": desc}
        out.append({"id": sid, "title": title, "description": desc, "scenario": sc,

"""

import argparse
import json
import os

from pathlib import Path

    try:

        main_env = (ROOT / common).resolve().parent / ".env"
        if main_env.exists():
            from dotenv import dotenv_values

            for k, v in dotenv_values(main_env).items():
                if v and not os.environ.get(k):
                    os.environ[k] = v
    except OSError:
        pass


load_env()

    )
    from neatlogs import span  # noqa: E402
else:

def tool_tracer(name: str, args: dict, fn):
    @span(kind="TOOL", name=f"tool.{name}", tool_name=name)
    def _call(tool_args: dict):
        return fn()

    return _call(args)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--variant", choices=["v1", "v2"], default="v2")
    ap.add_argument("--chaos", action="store_true", help="inject a model-checker crash to exercise recovery")

    ap.add_argument("--label", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)

    @span(kind="WORKFLOW", name=f"stop-prove.{args.variant}")
    def workflow(variant: str, chaos: bool) -> dict:
        return run_agent(variant, backend, chaos=chaos, max_steps=args.max_steps, tracer=tool_tracer)

    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    try:
        run = workflow(args.variant, args.chaos)
    finally:
        if NEATLOGS:
            neatlogs.flush()
    run["started_at"] = started
    doc = export_run(run, run_id, label, model, backend.name, os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_PROJECT_URL"))
    ev = doc["eval"]["repaired"]

        "id": run_id, "variant": args.variant, "chaos": args.chaos, "model": model, "backend": backend.name,
        "steps": len(run["steps"]), "llm_calls": run["llm_calls"], "duration_s": run["duration_s"],
        "tokens": run["tokens"], "cost_usd": run["cost_usd"],
        "visible": ev["visible"], "heldout": ev["heldout"], "faults_fixed": ev["faults_fixed"],
        "proven": sum(p["status"] == "proven" for p in ev["proofs"]), "fuzz_bad_episodes": ev["fuzz"]["violations"],
        "errors": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "error"),
        "recoveries": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "recover"),
        "rollbacks": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "rollback"),
    }
    out = ROOT / "docs" / "traces" / f"{run_id}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    if args.manifest:
        man = ROOT / "web" / "public" / "data" / "manifest.json"
        runs = json.loads(man.read_text())["runs"] if man.exists() else []
        runs = [(r["id"], r["label"]) for r in runs if r["id"] != run_id] + [(run_id, label)]
        write_manifest(runs, default=run_id if args.variant == "v2" and not args.chaos else (runs[0][0]))
    if NEATLOGS:
        neatlogs.shutdown()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Method:
1. Read the spec (machine, language, operating rules) and the program.
2. Run the tests. For each failure, read the details (scan tables) and form a root-cause hypothesis that names
   the rung(s) responsible. Use prove() to get the shortest counterexample for each violated safety rule.
   Use simulate() to confirm a hypothesis when the evidence is ambiguous.
3. Fix root causes with the smallest change that satisfies the rule as written. Batch related edits into one
   patch (max 4 edits). Never special-case test timings and never weaken a safety rule to make a test pass.
   The belt must stay useful: it has to run, deliver boxes and resume after a pick.
4. After every patch, read the test and proof results. If anything that passed before now fails, roll back
   and try a different fix.
5. Submit only when every visible test passes AND prove() reports S1-S6 PROVEN. In the summary, list each
   defect you found (rung, symptom, root cause) and the fix.
Be efficient: every tool call costs time and money."""


def _title(name: str, args: dict, result: str, ok: bool) -> str:
    first = result.splitlines()[0] if result else ""
    if not ok:
        return f"{name} failed: {result.removeprefix('ERROR: ')[:120]}"
    if name == "run_tests":
        return f"Run visible tests: {first.split(': ', 1)[-1]}"
    if name == "propose_patch":
        return first.replace("Patch applied as", "Patch applied:")
    if name == "prove":
        viol = [ln.split(":")[0] for ln in result.splitlines() if "VIOLATED" in ln]
        return "Prove S1-S6: " + ("all proven" if not viol else f"{', '.join(viol)} violated")
    if name == "get_test_details":
        return f"Inspect failing test {args.get('test_id', '')}"
    if name == "simulate":
        return f"Experiment on the digital twin ({len(args.get('events', []))} events)"
    if name == "rollback":
        return f"Roll back to {args.get('version', '')}"
    if name == "submit":
        return "Submit repaired program"
    if name == "read_spec":
        return "Read machine spec and operating rules"
    if name == "read_program":
        return "Read the program"
    return name


def _kind(name: str, ok: bool, prev_failed: bool) -> str:
    if not ok:
        return "error"
    if prev_failed:
        return "recover"
    return {"propose_patch": "patch", "rollback": "rollback", "submit": "submit"}.get(name, "tool")


def run_agent(variant: str, backend, *, chaos: bool = False, max_steps: int | None = None, tracer=None, log=print) -> dict:
    from .plc.cell import baseline_program

    v2 = variant == "v2"
    wb = Workbench(baseline_program(), verbose_results=v2, chaos=chaos)
    tools = [TOOL_DEFS[n] for n in (V2_TOOLS if v2 else V1_TOOLS)]
    system = SYSTEM_V2 if v2 else SYSTEM_V1
    max_steps = max_steps or (24 if v2 else 10)
    messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": TASK}]
    steps: list[dict] = []
    t0 = time.time()
    tokens_in = tokens_out = 0
    cost = 0.0
    prev_failed = False
    llm_calls = 0

    def add_step(**kw) -> None:
        kw.setdefault("program_version", wb.current)
        kw["i"] = len(steps) + 1
        kw["t"] = round(time.time() - t0, 2)
        steps.append(kw)

    for _ in range(max_steps):
        reply = backend.chat(system, messages, tools)
        llm_calls += 1
        tokens_in += reply.input_tokens
        tokens_out += reply.output_tokens
        cost += reply.cost_usd
        step_tokens = reply.input_tokens + reply.output_tokens
        if reply.text.strip():
            add_step(kind="think", title=reply.text.strip().splitlines()[0][:140], detail=reply.text.strip(),
                     tokens=step_tokens, cost_usd=round(reply.cost_usd, 5))
            step_tokens = 0
        if not reply.calls:
            messages.append(backend.assistant_message(reply))
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Act through exactly one tool call."})
            continue
        messages.append(backend.assistant_message(reply))
        for call in reply.calls:
            ok = True
            try:
                if tracer:
                    with tracer(call.name):
                        result = wb.call(call.name, call.args)
                else:
                    result = wb.call(call.name, call.args)
            except ToolFailure as e:
                ok, result = False, f"ERROR: {e}"
            except TypeError as e:  # wrong argument names from the model
                ok, result = False, f"ERROR: bad arguments for {call.name}: {e}"
            metrics = wb.metrics()
            add_step(kind=_kind(call.name, ok, prev_failed), tool=call.name, title=_title(call.name, call.args, result, ok),
                     detail=result[:4000], args=call.args, ok=ok, tokens=step_tokens or None, metrics=metrics)
            log(f"  [{variant}] {steps[-1]['title']}")
            step_tokens = 0
            prev_failed = not ok
            messages.append(backend.tool_message(call, result))
            if wb.submitted:
                break
        if wb.submitted:
            break

    if not wb.submitted:
        wb.submitted = wb.current
        wb.summary = "Step budget exhausted; the current version was submitted automatically."
        add_step(kind="submit", tool="submit", title="Step budget exhausted: auto-submit", detail=wb.summary, ok=False, metrics=wb.metrics())

    return {
        "variant": variant,
        "workbench": wb,
        "steps": steps,
        "summary": wb.summary,
        "final_version": wb.submitted,
        "duration_s": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
        "tokens": {"input": tokens_in, "output": tokens_out},
        "cost_usd": round(cost, 4),
        "llm_calls": llm_calls,
    }


class ScriptedBackend:
    """Test double that replays a fixed plan. Used only to test the pipeline offline; never published."""

    name = "scripted-test"
    model = "scripted"

    def __init__(self, plan: list[tuple[str, dict]]):
        self.plan = list(plan)
        self.i = 0

    def chat(self, system, messages, tools):
        from .llm import Reply, ToolCall

        name, args = self.plan[min(self.i, len(self.plan) - 1)]
        self.i += 1
        return Reply(f"(scripted) step {self.i}", [ToolCall(f"s{self.i}", name, args)], 0, 0, 0.0, 0.0)

    def assistant_message(self, reply):
        return {"role": "assistant", "content": json.dumps({"tool": reply.calls[0].name})}

    def tool_message(self, call, content):
        return {"role": "tool", "name": call.name, "content": content}

"""Run the STOP/PROVE agent on Cell 01, evaluate its repair on the held-out suite, and export the run.

    uv run python -m agent.run --variant v2                 # verified agent
    uv run python -m agent.run --variant v1                 # naive first version (the "before")
    uv run python -m agent.run --variant v2 --chaos         # inject a tool failure to show recovery
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def load_env() -> None:
    load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")
    # In a git worktree, fall back to the main checkout's .env for keys that are still empty.
    try:
        common = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
        main_env = (ROOT / common).resolve().parent / ".env"
        if main_env.exists():
            from dotenv import dotenv_values

            for k, v in dotenv_values(main_env).items():
                if v and not os.environ.get(k):
                    os.environ[k] = v
    except OSError:
        pass


load_env()

NEATLOGS = bool(os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"))
if NEATLOGS:
    import neatlogs  # noqa: E402  (must initialise before openai is imported)

    neatlogs.init(
        api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"],
        workflow_name="stop-prove",
        tags=["neathack", "stop-prove"],
        instrumentations=["openai"],
    )
    from neatlogs import span  # noqa: E402
else:
    def span(**_kw):  # no-op when neatlogs is not configured
        return lambda f: f

from .evaluate import export_run, write_manifest  # noqa: E402
from .llm import make_backend  # noqa: E402
from .loop import run_agent  # noqa: E402


def tool_tracer(name: str, args: dict, fn):
    @span(kind="TOOL", name=f"tool.{name}", tool_name=name)
    def _call(tool_args: dict):
        return fn()

    return _call(args)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--variant", choices=["v1", "v2"], default="v2")
    ap.add_argument("--chaos", action="store_true", help="inject a model-checker crash to exercise recovery")
    ap.add_argument("--id", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--label", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--backend", default=None, help="openai | claude-cli (default: openai when LLM_API_KEY is set)")
    ap.add_argument("--manifest", action="store_true", help="add this run to web/public/data/manifest.json")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    backend = make_backend(args.backend)
    model = getattr(backend, "model", "?")
    run_id = args.id or f"{args.variant}{'-chaos' if args.chaos else ''}-{datetime.now().strftime('%H%M')}"
    label = args.label or {
        "v1": "Agent v1 — naive (before)",
        "v2": "Agent v2 — verified (after)",
    }[args.variant] + (" + injected failure" if args.chaos else "")
    print(f"STOP/PROVE {args.variant} | backend={backend.name} model={model} | neatlogs={'on' if NEATLOGS else 'off'}")

    @span(kind="WORKFLOW", name=f"stop-prove.{args.variant}")
    def workflow(variant: str, chaos: bool) -> dict:
        return run_agent(variant, backend, chaos=chaos, max_steps=args.max_steps, tracer=tool_tracer)

    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    try:
        run = workflow(args.variant, args.chaos)
    finally:
        if NEATLOGS:
            neatlogs.flush()
    run["started_at"] = started
    doc = export_run(run, run_id, label, model, backend.name, os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_PROJECT_URL"))
    ev = doc["eval"]["repaired"]
    summary = {
        "id": run_id, "variant": args.variant, "chaos": args.chaos, "model": model, "backend": backend.name,
        "steps": len(run["steps"]), "llm_calls": run["llm_calls"], "duration_s": run["duration_s"],
        "tokens": run["tokens"], "cost_usd": run["cost_usd"],
        "visible": ev["visible"], "heldout": ev["heldout"], "faults_fixed": ev["faults_fixed"],
        "proven": sum(p["status"] == "proven" for p in ev["proofs"]), "fuzz_bad_episodes": ev["fuzz"]["violations"],
        "errors": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "error"),
        "recoveries": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "recover"),
        "rollbacks": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "rollback"),
    }
    out = ROOT / "docs" / "traces" / f"{run_id}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    if args.manifest:
        man = ROOT / "web" / "public" / "data" / "manifest.json"
        runs = json.loads(man.read_text())["runs"] if man.exists() else []
        runs = [(r["id"], r["label"]) for r in runs if r["id"] != run_id] + [(run_id, label)]
        write_manifest(runs, default=run_id if args.variant == "v2" and not args.chaos else (runs[0][0]))
    if NEATLOGS:
        neatlogs.shutdown()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

content.content:
# STOP/PROVE: business plan

> An AI agent that commissions PLC control logic before it touches a real machine. It tests the program against a digital twin, finds safety and functional bugs, proposes restricted patches, **proves** the safety rules with a model checker, and hands the controls engineer a verified patch plus an auditable report.

Team **LastCommit** (Mohammad Umar, Bilal Feroz Khan, Fuad Ahamed) · India · pre-seed · built at neatHack 2026 · plan dated 12 Oct 2026. Month 1 of the model is November 2026. All amounts are USD; INR at a planning rate of ₹95/USD.

# STOP/PROVE

> **An agent that commissions PLC logic, and proves it's safe.** Built live at **[neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)** (Oct 10–12, 2026) by team **LastCommit**. #neatHack

Every machine on a factory floor runs control logic that someone has to commission: test it, find the bugs, fix them, and sign it off. Today that happens on site, under time pressure, with real motors and real people nearby. The bugs that slip through are the dangerous kind. An E-stop clears itself without a reset. A belt restarts on its own when a guard door closes. A stuck sensor goes unnoticed.

STOP/PROVE does that commissioning job end to end, **before the logic touches a real machine**:

1. It gets a control program with **hidden, unlabelled faults**, plus the machine's operating rules.
2. It **tests** the program on a digital twin of the cell, reads the failures, and **runs its own experiments** to find root causes.
3. It **patches** the program in a restricted control language: small, reviewable edits that a validator checks.
4. It **proves** the safety rules with a model checker, across every reachable state and every possible input sequence. Passing the tests isn't enough.
5. It **recovers** when an action fails: rejected patches, regressions (rolled back) and tool crashes.
6. It **submits**, and an evaluation it never saw scores the repair: held-out tests, 300 randomized fuzz episodes and the proofs.

**Live demo:** _deploying_ · **Video:** _coming_ · **Business plan:** [docs/business-plan](docs/business-plan/README.md)

## What you see in the demo

- **The cell:** a high-poly three.js digital twin with an infeed conveyor, photo-eyes, an interlocked guard door, an operator panel, a stack light and a pick gantry. Every frame comes straight from the simulator.
- **Agent run:** the agent's real steps, one at a time. Tests and counterexamples, patches and rollbacks, failures and recoveries. The ladder-logic view diffs every program version.
- **Before / After:** the delivered program and the repaired one side by side on the same scenario. On the left a box gets pushed off the end; on the right the belt stops at the robot.
- **Play:** a live digital twin. Press START, slam the E-stop, open the guard, jam a sensor, or edit a rung yourself and watch the safety monitors.

## Results

| | Program as delivered | After the agent |
|---|---|---|
| Visible tests | 2 / 8 | _from the run_ |
| **Held-out tests** (never shown to the agent) | 2 / 16 | _from the run_ |
| Safety rules **proven** (S1–S6, every reachable state) | 3 / 6 | _from the run_ |
| Fuzz episodes with a violation (300 random runs) | 111 / 300 | _from the run_ |
| Hidden seeded faults fixed | 0 / 4 | _from the run_ |

Agent v1 vs v2 (before/after, traced in neatlogs): see [docs/traces](docs/traces/README.md).

## How it works

```
                 ┌──────────────── agent loop (agent/loop.py) ────────────────┐
  operating ───▶ │  read_spec · read_program · run_tests · get_test_details   │
  rules (S1–S7)  │  simulate (own experiments) · prove · propose_patch        │
  program v0 ──▶ │  rollback · submit                                         │
                 └───────┬───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                         │                               │
              digital twin (agent/plc)          model checker (agent/plc/verify.py)
              PLC scan engine + conveyor        every reachable state × all 128 input
              plant + safety monitors           combinations per scan, abstract timers
                         │                               │
                         └──────────▶  evaluation the agent never sees  ◀──────────┘
                                       held-out tests · 300 fuzz episodes · proofs
                                       · hidden fault manifest (agent/plc/hidden.py)
```

- **Restricted control language** ([agent/plc/lang.py](agent/plc/lang.py)): assignments, SET/RESET latches, on-delay timers and rising edges, within 24 rungs, 4 timers and 12 contacts per rung. The agent can only change the program through validated patches of at most 4 edits.
- **Digital twin** ([agent/plc/engine.py](agent/plc/engine.py), [sim.py](agent/plc/sim.py)): a deterministic scan engine (0.1 s scan) and a conveyor plant in integer millimetres. The same simulator is ported to TypeScript for the browser, and [scripts/parity_check.py](scripts/parity_check.py) checks the two produce identical traces.
- **Proofs** ([agent/plc/verify.py](agent/plc/verify.py)): explicit-state model checking. All 7 inputs are free every scan, so stuck sensors and any operator behaviour are covered. Timers are abstracted, so a running timer may finish at any later scan, which makes a proven rule hold for every timer preset and every sequence length. A violation comes back as the shortest counterexample.
- **Hidden answer:** the agent gets the executable model and test results, never the fault labels or the held-out suite.

### The seeded faults (spoilers)

<details><summary>What the agent had to find</summary>

| Fault | Rung | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| Missing E-stop reset | R02 | The E-stop latch clears on release; no RESET needed (violates S5) |
| Timing race at the pick position | R07/R08 | PE_END is debounced for 1.2 s, but the box reaches the end of the belt in 0.8 s, so it falls off (violates S6) |
| Unsupervised stuck sensor | R03 | The jam timer runs while the motor is OFF: a stuck PE_IN is never caught, and a waiting box raises a false alarm (violates S7) |
| Restart after the guard closes | R06 | Opening the guard doesn't drop run mode, so closing it restarts the belt (violates S4) |

</details>

## Built with

| Tool | How it's used |
|---|---|
| [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) | Traces every agent run: the workflow span, every LLM call and every tool call, with tokens, latency and cost. The before/after comparison of agent v1 and v2 is in [docs/traces](docs/traces/README.md). |
| [Entire](https://entire.io) | Records the Claude Code session behind this repo's commits as checkpoints. |
| [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) | The business plan: pricing, costs, revenue and runway ([docs/business-plan](docs/business-plan/README.md)). |
| Claude (via the neatHack LiteLLM proxy) | The agent's model. |
| three.js | The digital twin (all CC0 assets from Poly Haven, see `web/public/assets/CREDITS.txt`). |

## Run it

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env                                   # LLM_API_KEY (+ NEATLOGS_API_KEY for traces)
uv run python -m agent.run --variant v2 --manifest     # verified agent, exported to the viewer
uv run python -m agent.run --variant v1 --manifest     # naive first version, for the before/after
uv run python -m agent.run --variant v2 --chaos        # injected tool failure, to show recovery
uv run python -m scripts.check_cell                    # tests, fuzz and proofs on the baseline and a reference fix
cd web && npm install && npm run dev                   # the viewer at http://localhost:5173
```

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `agent/plc/` | Language, scan engine, plant, monitors, simulator, tests, model checker, hidden scoring data |
| `agent/loop.py`, `agent/tools.py`, `agent/llm.py` | The agent: loop, tools, LLM backends |
| `agent/run.py`, `agent/evaluate.py` | Run, held-out evaluation, export to `web/public/data` |
| `web/` | The viewer: three.js digital twin (`src/scene`), UI (`src/ui`), browser simulator (`src/sim`) |
| `docs/` | Business plan, traces, build log |

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# STOP/PROVE

> **An agent that commissions PLC logic, and proves it's safe.** Built live at **[neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)** (Oct 10–12, 2026) by team **LastCommit**. #neatHack

Every machine on a factory floor runs control logic that someone has to commission: test it, find the bugs, fix them, and sign it off. Today that happens on site, under time pressure, with real motors and real people nearby. The bugs that slip through are the dangerous kind. An E-stop clears itself without a reset. A belt restarts on its own when a guard door closes. A stuck sensor goes unnoticed.

STOP/PROVE does that commissioning job end to end, **before the logic touches a real machine**:

1. It gets a control program with **hidden, unlabelled faults**, plus the machine's operating rules.
2. It **tests** the program on a digital twin of the cell, reads the failures, and **runs its own experiments** to find root causes.
3. It **patches** the program in a restricted control language: small, reviewable edits that a validator checks.
4. It **proves** the safety rules with a model checker, across every reachable state and every possible input sequence. Passing the tests isn't enough.
5. It **recovers** when an action fails: rejected patches, regressions (rolled back) and tool crashes.
6. It **submits**, and an evaluation it never saw scores the repair: held-out tests, 300 randomized fuzz episodes and the proofs.

**Live demo:** _deploying_ · **Video:** _coming_ · **Business plan:** [docs/business-plan](docs/business-plan/README.md)

## What you see in the demo

- **The cell:** a high-poly three.js digital twin with an infeed conveyor, photo-eyes, an interlocked guard door, an operator panel, a stack light and a pick gantry. Every frame comes straight from the simulator.
- **Agent run:** the agent's real steps, one at a time. Tests and counterexamples, patches and rollbacks, failures and recoveries. The ladder-logic view diffs every program version.
- **Before / After:** the delivered program and the repaired one side by side on the same scenario. On the left a box gets pushed off the end; on the right the belt stops at the robot.
- **Play:** a live digital twin. Press START, slam the E-stop, open the guard, jam a sensor, or edit a rung yourself and watch the safety monitors.

# /brag

You built it. Now let's brag about it.

## Invocation dispatch (must happen first)

**Model check.** If you are Claude Opus 5.5 and the invocation doesn't ask for the full workflow (`--full`, "use the full brag") or for voiceover (`--voice`, which brag-slim doesn't do), switch to brag-slim: read `<skill-dir>/slim.md` (the /brag-slim skill, bundled here) and follow it for the rest of this run instead of this file. Pass along the user's input, and pass any other options (`--no-music`, `--title`, …) as plain-language direction. Tell the user in one line first, e.g. "You're on Opus 5.5, so I'm using /brag-slim: I build the whole video myself. Say 'use the full brag' to switch back." If you are any other model, or can't tell which model you are, skip this check.

Before inspecting the project, parse the complete `/brag` invocation. If the
invocation contains `--voice`, set `voice.enabled = true`. Enable narration
only for that run. Do not enable narration automatically and do not fall back
to the normal no-voice workflow.

`/brag` turns the current project website or app into a short, polished, shareable launch video using Hyperframes. It is narrow, opinionated, and fun.

## What this skill does

1. Reads the current project code to understand the app.
2. Plans a short brag concept specific to this project.
3. Scripts and storyboards the video.
4. Hands a focused composition brief to Hyperframes.
5. Validates, renders, and writes share copy.

## Parsing the invocation

The user may invoke with natural language or flags:

```
/brag
/brag --tone chaotic
/brag --tone polished --format vertical
/brag this. Make it feel like a ridiculous startup launch.
```

Parse these options:

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--tone` | preset or freeform description | inferred |
| `--format` | `landscape`, `vertical`, `square` | `landscape` |
| `--duration` | seconds | auto (15-25s) |
| `--no-music` | flag | music on |
| `--no-sfx` | flag | sfx on |
| `--title` | string | inferred from project |
| `--voice` | flag | narration off |

Voice is opt-in. If `--voice` is present, use Kokoro via Hyperframes and do
not add any provider-selection logic. The voice workflow is intentionally
single-provider.

Tone can be a preset (`default`, `polished`, `yc-parody`, `chaotic`, `deadpan`, `cinematic`, `app-store`) or a creative direction such as "fake Series A launch from 2016", "museum exhibit", or "overproduced mobile game ad".

When the user gives freeform tone direction, map it to the nearest preset for pacing and structure, but preserve the user's direction in the plan and composition brief.

## Narration guidance

When `--voice` is enabled, write narration that complements the visuals, does
not simply read visible text, matches scene pacing, sounds natural and
conversational, and moves smoothly between scenes. Keep the script concise and
specific to the product so the voice feels like part of the edit rather than a
separate narration track.

---

## Output directory

By default, output goes to `brag-output/`. To avoid overwriting previous runs, use a timestamped directory:

```
brag-output-2026-05-04-143022/
```

Use a timestamp when:
- The user explicitly asks for a new run without overriding previous results
- A `brag-output/` directory already exists in the project

Generate the timestamp at the start of the run (`YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss`) and use it consistently for all output paths in that run: plan, brief, composition, render, and share copy.

## Skill directory

`<skill-dir>` is the directory containing this `SKILL.md`. Claude Code prints it as "Base directory for this skill" when the skill loads; for other agents it's wherever the skill was installed. Bundled assets are under `<skill-dir>/assets/` and scripts under `<skill-dir>/scripts/`. Don't guess an install path: a plugin install, a `~/.claude/skills/` copy, and this repo all put it somewhere different.

---

## Step 1: Inspect the project

**Read:** [references/step-1-inspect.md](references/step-1-inspect.md)

Scan the project directory and extract the information needed to plan the brag video.

**Gate:** You can answer all 9 questions in the brag planning rubric.

---

## Step 2: Plan and storyboard

**Read:** [references/step-2-plan.md](references/step-2-plan.md)

Write `<output-dir>/brag-plan.md` (where `<output-dir>` is `brag-output/` or the timestamped variant chosen above). Answer the planning rubric. Commit to a creative angle. Write the beat-by-beat storyboard including scenes, text, timing, transitions, and SFX cues.

When music is selected, include a compact `Music cue guidance` section: read the bundled track's cue preset from `<skill-dir>/assets/music/cues/` if present, otherwise note cues will be detected at composition time (any track now supports beat sync — see `references/audio.md`). Cue metadata is optional timing guidance only: story, readability, pacing, and product clarity stay primary.

**Gate:** `<output-dir>/brag-plan.md` exists with a full storyboard. Scene durations sum to 15–25 seconds.

---

## Step 3: Hand off to Hyperframes

**Read:** The Hyperframes domain skills — `hyperframes-core`, `hyperframes-animation`, `hyperframes-creative`, `hyperframes-keyframes`, `hyperframes-cli`. /brag is its own workflow: do not enter the `hyperframes` entry-point intent interview or route into its generic promo / launch-video workflow.
**Read:** [references/step-3-compose.md](references/step-3-compose.md)
**Read:** [references/audio.md](references/audio.md)

Write the composition brief and use Hyperframes to create the video implementation in `<output-dir>/composition/`.

`/brag` owns the product angle, source material, storyboard, tone, format, audio selection, music cue guidance, and delivery expectations. Hyperframes owns the concrete composition structure, exact animation timing, animation mechanics, runtime choices, linting rules, and render workflow.

**Gate:** `npx hyperframes check` passes with zero errors inside `<output-dir>/composition/` (the single browser gate before render — see hyperframes-cli for what it audits).

---

## Step 4: Validate, render, and deliver

**Read:** [references/step-4-deliver.md](references/step-4-deliver.md)

Validate, preview, render to `<output-dir>/brag.mp4`, pick the best poster frame into `<output-dir>/brag.jpg`, bake that poster as the video's frame 0 so it's the idle thumbnail everywhere, and write `<output-dir>/share-copy.txt`.

**Gate:** `<output-dir>/brag.mp4` exists. A best-frame poster `<output-dir>/brag.jpg` is picked (not an arbitrary frame) and baked as frame 0 of `brag.mp4`. Share copy is written.

---

## Tone system

Seven tone presets ship with `/brag`. Each changes scripting energy, pacing, typography personality, and transition style. Presets are defaults, not limits.

Full definitions: [references/tones.md](references/tones.md)

| Tone | Energy | One-liner |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | Playful, clean, postable | The good-vibes default |
| `polished` | Serious, elegant | For projects that are not jokes |
| `yc-parody` | Deadpan startup energy | Fake seriousness applied to absurd projects |
| `chaotic` | Fast, loud, aggressive | Over-the-top and unhinged |
| `deadpan` | Calm, dry, understated | The joke is that nothing is a joke |
| `cinematic` | Dramatic, trailer-scale | Big motion, bigger claims |
| `app-store` | Smooth, feature-card clean | Corporate but not boring |

Always allow a freeform creative direction to refine or override the preset.

---

## Creative laws

These apply to every brag video regardless of tone.

**Short.** 15–25 seconds. Not one second more without a reason.

**Readable.** Keep the pace high through motion and cuts, never by flashing text. Every line a viewer must read holds long enough to read it (short label ~0.8s settled; a sentence ~0.3s per word). Fast-in, then hold — never fast-in, then gone.

**Specific.** The video must feel like it was made for this exact project, not any project.

**Show the thing.** At least one scene must display actual UI, copy, or a key visual from the product. No abstract filler.

**No generic SaaS language.** "Streamline your workflow" is banned. Use the project's actual copy and claims.

**The hook is everything.** The first 2 seconds determine whether someone keeps watching. Plan the hook before anything else.

**Funny earns its place.** Humor should come from the project's absurdity, not from trying to be funny.

**Pattern:**
```
Hook (2-3s) → Reveal (2-4s) → 2-3 sharp highlights (5-12s) → Punchline/outro (2-4s)
```

Adapt this. Not every project needs exactly 3 highlights. The pattern is a starting shape, not a template.

"""The STOP/PROVE agent loop: plan, act through tools, verify, recover, submit.

v1 is the naive first version (tests only, pass/fail answers, no verification). v2 adds failure
details, experiments on the digital twin, the model checker, regression detection and rollback."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time

from .tools import TOOL_DEFS, V1_TOOLS, V2_TOOLS, ToolFailure, Workbench

TASK = (
    "You are commissioning the control program for Cell 01, an infeed conveyor, before it is loaded into the real PLC. "
    "The program was written by a contractor and has not been verified. Make it satisfy every operating rule. "
    "Start by reading the spec and the program."
)

SYSTEM_V1 = (
    "You are a PLC programmer. Fix the program so that the tests pass, using the tools. "
    "Submit when you are done."
)

SYSTEM_V2 = """You are STOP/PROVE, a careful controls engineer agent. You commission PLC logic on a digital twin before it
touches a real machine. The program you are given has an unknown number of defects. Nobody will tell you what
they are: find them from evidence.

Method:
1. Read the spec (machine, language, operating rules) and the program.
2. Run the tests. For each failure, read the details (scan tables) and form a root-cause hypothesis that names
   the rung(s) responsible. Use prove() to get the shortest counterexample for each violated safety rule.
   Use simulate() to confirm a hypothesis when the evidence is ambiguous.
3. Fix root causes with the smallest change that satisfies the rule as written. Batch related edits into one
   patch (max 4 edits). Never special-case test timings and never weaken a safety rule to make a test pass.
   The belt must stay useful: it has to run, deliver boxes and resume after a pick.
4. After every patch, read the test and proof results. If anything that passed before now fails, roll back
   and try a different fix.
5. Submit only when every visible test passes AND prove() reports S1-S6 PROVEN. In the summary, list each
   defect you found (rung, symptom, root cause) and the fix.
Be efficient: every tool call costs time and money."""


def _title(name: str, args: dict, result: str, ok: bool) -> str:
    first = result.splitlines()[0] if result else ""
    if not ok:
        return f"{name} failed: {result.removeprefix('ERROR: ')[:120]}"
    if name == "run_tests":
        return f"Run visible tests: {first.split(': ', 1)[-1]}"
    if name == "propose_patch":
        return first.replace("Patch applied as", "Patch applied:")
    if name == "prove":
        viol = [ln.split(":")[0] for ln in result.splitlines() if "VIOLATED" in ln]
        return "Prove S1-S6: " + ("all proven" if not viol else f"{', '.join(viol)} violated")
    if name == "get_test_details":
        return f"Inspect failing test {args.get('test_id', '')}"
    if name == "simulate":
        return f"Experiment on the digital twin ({len(args.get('events', []))} events)"
    if name == "rollback":
        return f"Roll back to {args.get('version', '')}"
    if name == "submit":
        return "Submit repaired program"
    if name == "read_spec":
        return "Read machine spec and operating rules"
    if name == "read_program":
        return "Read the program"
    return name


def _kind(name: str, ok: bool, prev_failed: bool) -> str:
    if not ok:
        return "error"
    if prev_failed:
        return "recover"
    return {"propose_patch": "patch", "rollback": "rollback", "submit": "submit"}.get(name, "tool")


def run_agent(variant: str, backend, *, chaos: bool = False, max_steps: int | None = None, tracer=None, log=print) -> dict:
    from .plc.cell import baseline_program

    v2 = variant == "v2"
    wb = Workbench(baseline_program(), verbose_results=v2, chaos=chaos)
    tools = [TOOL_DEFS[n] for n in (V2_TOOLS if v2 else V1_TOOLS)]
    system = SYSTEM_V2 if v2 else SYSTEM_V1
    max_steps = max_steps or (24 if v2 else 10)
    messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": TASK}]
    steps: list[dict] = []
    t0 = time.time()
    tokens_in = tokens_out = 0
    cost = 0.0
    prev_failed = False
    llm_calls = 0

    def add_step(**kw) -> None:
        kw.setdefault("program_version", wb.current)
        kw["i"] = len(steps) + 1
        kw["t"] = round(time.time() - t0, 2)
        steps.append(kw)

    for _ in range(max_steps):
        reply = backend.chat(system, messages, tools)
        llm_calls += 1
        tokens_in += reply.input_tokens
        tokens_out += reply.output_tokens
        cost += reply.cost_usd
        step_tokens = reply.input_tokens + reply.output_tokens
        if reply.text.strip():
            add_step(kind="think", title=reply.text.strip().splitlines()[0][:140], detail=reply.text.strip(),
                     tokens=step_tokens, cost_usd=round(reply.cost_usd, 5))
            step_tokens = 0
        if not reply.calls:
            messages.append(backend.assistant_message(reply))
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Act through exactly one tool call."})
            continue
        messages.append(backend.assistant_message(reply))
        for call in reply.calls:
            ok = True
            try:
                if tracer:
                    result = tracer(call.name, call.args, lambda: wb.call(call.name, call.args))
                else:
                    result = wb.call(call.name, call.args)
            except ToolFailure as e:
                ok, result = False, f"ERROR: {e}"
            except TypeError as e:  # wrong argument names from the model
                ok, result = False, f"ERROR: bad arguments for {call.name}: {e}"
            metrics = wb.metrics()
            add_step(kind=_kind(call.name, ok, prev_failed), tool=call.name, title=_title(call.name, call.args, result, ok),
                     detail=result[:4000], args=call.args, ok=ok, tokens=step_tokens or None, metrics=metrics)
            log(f"  [{variant}] {steps[-1]['title']}")
            step_tokens = 0
            prev_failed = not ok
            messages.append(backend.tool_message(call, result))
            if wb.submitted:
                break
        if wb.submitted:
            break

    if not wb.submitted:
        wb.submitted = wb.current
        wb.summary = "Step budget exhausted; the current version was submitted automatically."
        add_step(kind="submit", tool="submit", title="Step budget exhausted: auto-submit", detail=wb.summary, ok=False, metrics=wb.metrics())

    return {
        "variant": variant,
        "workbench": wb,
        "steps": steps,
        "summary": wb.summary,
        "final_version": wb.submitted,
        "duration_s": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
        "tokens": {"input": tokens_in, "output": tokens_out},
        "cost_usd": round(cost, 4),
        "llm_calls": llm_calls,
    }


class ScriptedBackend:
    """Test double that replays a fixed plan. Used only to test the pipeline offline; never published."""

    name = "scripted-test"
    model = "scripted"

    def __init__(self, plan: list[tuple[str, dict]]):
        self.plan = list(plan)
        self.i = 0

    def chat(self, system, messages, tools):
        from .llm import Reply, ToolCall

        name, args = self.plan[min(self.i, len(self.plan) - 1)]
        self.i += 1
        return Reply(f"(scripted) step {self.i}", [ToolCall(f"s{self.i}", name, args)], 0, 0, 0.0, 0.0)

    def assistant_message(self, reply):
        return {"role": "assistant", "content": json.dumps({"tool": reply.calls[0].name})}

    def tool_message(self, call, content):
        return {"role": "tool", "name": call.name, "content": content}

from scripts.pipeline_test import plan

STATE = {"i": 0, "errors": []}

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def do_POST(self):
        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        msgs = body["messages"]

"""Run the STOP/PROVE agent on Cell 01, evaluate its repair on the held-out suite, and export the run.

    uv run python -m agent.run --variant v2                 # verified agent
    uv run python -m agent.run --variant v1                 # naive first version (the "before")
    uv run python -m agent.run --variant v2 --chaos         # inject a tool failure to show recovery
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def load_env() -> None:
    load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")
    # In a git worktree, fall back to the main checkout's .env for keys that are still empty.
    try:
        common = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
        main_env = (ROOT / common).resolve().parent / ".env"
        if main_env.exists():
            from dotenv import dotenv_values

            for k, v in dotenv_values(main_env).items():
                if v and not os.environ.get(k):
                    os.environ[k] = v
    except OSError:
        pass


load_env()

NEATLOGS = bool(os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"))
if NEATLOGS:
    import neatlogs  # noqa: E402  (must initialise before openai is imported)

    neatlogs.init(
        api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"],
        workflow_name="stop-prove",
        tags=["neathack", "stop-prove"],
        instrumentations=["openai"],
    )
    from neatlogs import span  # noqa: E402
else:
    def span(**_kw):  # no-op when neatlogs is not configured
        return lambda f: f

from .evaluate import export_run, write_manifest  # noqa: E402
from .llm import make_backend  # noqa: E402
from .loop import run_agent  # noqa: E402


def tool_tracer(name: str, args: dict, fn):
    @span(kind="TOOL", name=f"tool.{name}", tool_name=name)
    def _call(tool_args: dict):
        return fn()

    return _call(args)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--variant", choices=["v1", "v2"], default="v2")
    ap.add_argument("--chaos", action="store_true", help="inject a model-checker crash to exercise recovery")
    ap.add_argument("--id", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--label", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--backend", default=None, help="openai | claude-cli (default: openai when LLM_API_KEY is set)")
    ap.add_argument("--manifest", action="store_true", help="add this run to web/public/data/manifest.json")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    backend = make_backend(args.backend)
    model = getattr(backend, "model", "?")
    run_id = args.id or f"{args.variant}{'-chaos' if args.chaos else ''}-{datetime.now().strftime('%H%M')}"
    label = args.label or {
        "v1": "Agent v1 — naive (before)",
        "v2": "Agent v2 — verified (after)",
    }[args.variant] + (" + injected failure" if args.chaos else "")
    print(f"STOP/PROVE {args.variant} | backend={backend.name} model={model} | neatlogs={'on' if NEATLOGS else 'off'}")

    @span(kind="WORKFLOW", name=f"stop-prove.{args.variant}")
    def workflow(variant: str, chaos: bool) -> dict:
        return run_agent(variant, backend, chaos=chaos, max_steps=args.max_steps, tracer=tool_tracer)

    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    try:
        run = workflow(args.variant, args.chaos)
    finally:
        if NEATLOGS:
            neatlogs.flush()
    run["started_at"] = started
    doc = export_run(run, run_id, label, model, backend.name, os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_PROJECT_URL"))
    ev = doc["eval"]["repaired"]
    summary = {
        "id": run_id, "variant": args.variant, "chaos": args.chaos, "model": model, "backend": backend.name,
        "steps": len(run["steps"]), "llm_calls": run["llm_calls"], "duration_s": run["duration_s"],
        "tokens": run["tokens"], "cost_usd": run["cost_usd"],
        "visible": ev["visible"], "heldout": ev["heldout"], "faults_fixed": ev["faults_fixed"],
        "proven": sum(p["status"] == "proven" for p in ev["proofs"]), "fuzz_bad_episodes": ev["fuzz"]["violations"],
        "errors": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "error"),
        "recoveries": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "recover"),
        "rollbacks": sum(1 for s in run["steps"] if s["kind"] == "rollback"),
    }
    out = ROOT / "docs" / "traces" / f"{run_id}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    if args.manifest:
        man = ROOT / "web" / "public" / "data" / "manifest.json"
        runs = json.loads(man.read_text())["runs"] if man.exists() else []
        runs = [(r["id"], r["label"]) for r in runs if r["id"] != run_id] + [(run_id, label)]
        write_manifest(runs, default=run_id if args.variant == "v2" and not args.chaos else (runs[0][0]))
    if NEATLOGS:
        neatlogs.shutdown()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Build log (#neatHack)

Public log of the build. Times are IST.

| When (Oct 12) | Update | Post |
|---|---|---|
| 12:00 | Repo and tooling set up: neatlogs SDK, Entire checkpoints for Claude Code, Python + uv. | |
| 16:00 | Idea locked: **STOP/PROVE**, an agent that commissions PLC logic for a conveyor cell and proves the safety rules before the logic reaches a machine. | |
| 16:15 | Data contract between the Python agent and the web viewer (`web/src/types.ts`). Three parallel Claude Code subagents start: the 3D digital twin, the viewer UI with an in-browser simulator, and the business plan. | |
| 17:00–18:15 | High-poly three.js cell: T-slot conveyor, photo-eyes with live beams, interlocked guard door, operator panel, stack light, pick gantry, Poly Haven HDRI and textures. Viewer: agent timeline, ladder-logic view with diffs and live power flow, logic analyzer, Before/After twin mode, Play mode. | |
| 18:20 | Python core: restricted control language, scan engine, conveyor plant, safety monitors. It produces identical traces to the TypeScript simulator on all 10 golden scenarios. | |
| 18:35 | Test suites (8 visible, 16 held-out, randomized fuzzing) and a model checker with timer abstraction. Program as delivered: 2/16 held-out, 3/6 rules proven. Reference repair: 16/16, 6/6, in 0.5 s. | |
| 18:50 | Agent loop with 9 tools, v1 (naive) and v2 (verified) configurations, injected-failure mode, context trimming, held-out evaluation and export to the viewer. Tested offline with a scripted backend and a mock OpenAI-compatible server. | |
| 19:00 | GitHub Pages workflow, demo-video recorder (headless Chrome screencast), Kokoro voice-over test. | |

## Problems hit (and what we did)

- **Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` hook hangs** in this setup (Claude Code running in a git worktree with background subagents). Commits stall until the hook process is stopped. Entire also registered the session against the main checkout, so it reports "no files modified" and records no checkpoints for work done in the worktree. Plan: move the final commits to a session opened in the main checkout.
- **No model access while the team lead was away**: the LiteLLM key needs every teammate's web check-in, and the local Claude CLI's login had expired. The agent was built and tested offline (scripted backend, mock OpenAI server) so the real runs take minutes once a key is in place.

# Launch posts (drafts: nothing here is posted until Umar approves)

## LinkedIn

We spent this weekend at #neatHack building STOP/PROVE: an AI agent that commissions PLC control logic, and proves it's safe, before the logic ever touches a real machine.

Every conveyor, palletiser and robot cell runs control logic that someone has to commission on site, next to real motors and real people. The bugs that slip through are the dangerous kind: an E-stop that clears itself, a belt that restarts when a guard door closes, a stuck sensor nobody supervises.

STOP/PROVE gets a control program with hidden faults it is never told about. It:
→ tests the program on a digital twin of the cell (live 3D, in the browser)
→ reads the failures and runs its own experiments to find root causes
→ patches the program in a restricted, validated control language
→ proves every safety rule with a model checker: all reachable states, every input sequence, not just "the tests passed"
→ recovers when an action fails, then submits
An evaluation it never sees scores the repair: held-out tests, 300 randomized fuzz runs and the proofs.

Built with neatlogs (every agent run traced, so v1 vs v2 is measured, not guessed), Entire (the coding-agent sessions behind the commits) and cfo.ai (pricing, costs and runway).

Team LastCommit: Mohammad Umar, Bilal Feroz Khan, Fuad Ahamed.

Demo: <LIVE URL>
Code: https://github.com/Mohammad-Umar7/neathack-agent

#neatHack #AIagents #IndustrialAutomation #PLC #DigitalTwin

Hidden faults → tests on a 3D digital twin → patches → proofs → held-out score.
Repo: https://github.com/Mohammad-Umar7/neathack-agent
Demo: <LIVE URL> · Video: <attached>

# Step 3: Hand off to Hyperframes

## Create the composition brief

Write `<output-dir>/composition-brief.md` before creating or editing the Hyperframes composition.

```markdown
# Hyperframes Composition Brief: [App Name]

## Objective
Create a short launch-style brag video for [App Name].

## Output
- Composition directory: `<output-dir>/composition/`
- Rendered video: `<output-dir>/brag.mp4`
- Format: [landscape / vertical / square] — [width]x[height]
- Duration: [15-25 seconds]

## Source Material
- Project root: [path]
- Primary files read: [index.html, styles.css, README, etc.]
- Product name: [name]
- Tagline / strongest claim: [line]
- Key UI or visual moment to recreate: [specific element]
- Copy that must appear verbatim:
  - [line 1]
  - [line 2]

## Creative Direction
- Tone preset: [default / polished / yc-parody / chaotic / deadpan / cinematic / app-store]
- Creative direction: [freeform phrase, inferred or user-provided]
- Interpretation: [how tone affects pacing, writing, visual energy, and restraint]
- Angle: [one paragraph from brag-plan.md]
- Hook: [first 2-3 seconds]
- Outro / punchline: [final line]
- Avoid:
  - Generic SaaS language
  - Abstract filler visuals
  - Unrelated visual redesign

## Visual Identity
- Background: [exact value from project]
- Text: [exact value from project]
- Accent: [exact value from project]
- Display font: [font or fallback decision]
- Body font: [font or fallback decision]
- Visual references from the project: [short list]

## Storyboard
Use the storyboard in `<output-dir>/brag-plan.md` as the creative contract.

Scene summary:
1. [Scene name] — [duration]s — [what must be seen / read]
2. [Scene name] — [duration]s — [what must be seen / read]
3. [...]

## Audio
- Audio role: [warm bed / sparse professional accents / cinematic support / dense rhythmic layer / intentional silence]
- Audio arc: [how sound changes across the video]
- Music: [filename, or none only if disabled, missing, or intentionally silent]
# Step 4: Validate, render, and deliver

## Validate

```bash
cd <output-dir>/composition
npx hyperframes check   # brag's single pre-render gate — fix every error it reports
```

Fix all errors. `check` is brag's single pre-render gate — run it and fix everything it reports, including WCAG contrast failures (they gate as errors, not warnings). Each contrast finding carries a suggested compliant color, so apply it or adjust within the palette family and re-run `check` — most fixes need no screenshot. There is no per-element contrast escape hatch for real text; the only bypass is `check --no-contrast`, which skips the entire WCAG pass (all-or-nothing), not a way to accept one borderline element. For exact contrast thresholds, layout escape hatches, and reporting details, follow the current hyperframes-cli `check` guidance. `check`'s layout pass backstops the "keep all text readable" creative law — fix any reported overflow.

For a visual gut-check before rendering, optionally capture key frames:

```bash
npx hyperframes snapshot   # PNG key frames
```

## Preview

```bash
npx hyperframes preview
```

Tell the user the preview is running and give them the localhost URL. Invite them to check it before rendering.

If the user approves or asks to render:

## Render

```bash
npx hyperframes render --output ../brag.mp4
```

This outputs to `<output-dir>/brag.mp4` (one level up from the composition directory).

For a faster iteration render:
```bash
npx hyperframes render --quality draft --output ../brag.mp4
```

last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

# /brag

You built it. Now let's brag about it.

## Invocation dispatch (must happen first)

**Model check.** If you are Claude Opus 5.5 and the invocation doesn't ask for the full workflow (`--full`, "use the full brag") or for voiceover (`--voice`, which brag-slim doesn't do), switch to brag-slim: read `<skill-dir>/slim.md` (the /brag-slim skill, bundled here) and follow it for the rest of this run instead of this file. Pass along the user's input, and pass any other options (`--no-music`, `--title`, …) as plain-language direction. Tell the user in one line first, e.g. "You're on Opus 5.5, so I'm using /brag-slim: I build the whole video myself. Say 'use the full brag' to switch back." If you are any other model, or can't tell which model you are, skip this check.

Before inspecting the project, parse the complete `/brag` invocation. If the
invocation contains `--voice`, set `voice.enabled = true`. Enable narration
only for that run. Do not enable narration automatically and do not fall back
to the normal no-voice workflow.

`/brag` turns the current project website or app into a short, polished, shareable launch video using Hyperframes. It is narrow, opinionated, and fun.

## What this skill does

1. Reads the current project code to understand the app.
2. Plans a short brag concept specific to this project.
3. Scripts and storyboards the video.
4. Hands a focused composition brief to Hyperframes.
5. Validates, renders, and writes share copy.

## Parsing the invocation

The user may invoke with natural language or flags:

```
/brag
/brag --tone chaotic
/brag --tone polished --format vertical
/brag this. Make it feel like a ridiculous startup launch.
```

Parse these options:

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--tone` | preset or freeform description | inferred |
| `--format` | `landscape`, `vertical`, `square` | `landscape` |

| `--no-sfx` | flag | sfx on |
